failure_summary.description: The selected option did not match the strongest theorem-supported claim: most choices underclaimed, while some added unsupported quantitative or asymptotic strength.

patch.reasoning: The recurring issue is not a particular theorem but failure to compare the exact logical strength of the choices. A disciplined comparison should preserve conditions and scope, choose the strongest claim actually supported, and avoid treating the numerically largest bound as automatically true.

edits.content:
## Choosing the Strongest Valid Option
- Rewrite each choice as a claim, preserving its antecedents, quantifiers, domain, time range, and regularity. Compare the claims by logical implication, not by how confident or detailed they sound.
- Choose the strongest claim entailed by the hypotheses and established result: do not stop at a safe weaker conclusion, but do not add an unproved strengthening either. A conditional conclusion may be stronger and valid as stated; retain its condition rather than silently treating it as already satisfied.
- Check distinctions such as local versus global, eventual versus finite-time, interior-time versus endpoint regularity, and a property versus a strictly stronger property. Extra coefficients, rates, or other precise details require their own support.

## Comparing Quantitative Bounds
When choices assert bounds in the same direction, identify which numerical threshold makes the claim stronger, then separately verify which threshold is actually established. Do not select the largest displayed number merely because it is the strongest-looking estimate; the strongest valid bound may be weaker. Use the applicable known result precisely and do not infer an improvement that has not been proved.
